title: Motion Optimization + Controller Dialect Engine
description: Wire Phase 3 (motion optimization) and build the critical ControllerDialectEngine. Motion stages ensure commanded feeds are actually achievable given machine dynamics (acceleration, jerk, corner velocity, servo settling). The ControllerDialectEngine provides deep G-code dialect knowledge for 15+ controller families — canned cycles, work offsets, sub-programs, rotary axis conventions, tool change sequences, and controller-specific optimization codes (AICC, Cycle32, G187, etc.).

units.title: Stage 3.1-3.2 — Toolpath smoothing + Motion dynamics (achievable feed calculation)
steps: Wire ToolpathSmoothingEngine: apply B-spline/Bézier/corner-round smoothing to linear segments
Calculate curvature κ at every point using Frenet-Serret formulas
Curvature-limited feed: v_max = √(a_centripetal / κ) — feed can't exceed what the machine can track
Wire MotionDynamicsProfileEngine: calculate achievable feed per block
Trapezoidal velocity profile: accel phase, cruise phase, decel phase — actual time ≠ distance/feed
S-curve profiles: jerk-limited acceleration for smooth motion (Siemens/Heidenhain prefer this)
Corner velocity: decelerate before corners based on angle change and machine accel capability
If commanded feed > achievable feed, clamp to achievable and log the limiting factor
Short segment detection: segments < 0.5mm may not reach commanded feed — warn about block starvation
exit_conditions: Curvature-limited feeds are lower at tight corners
Achievable feed < commanded feed for short segments (proves physics is active)
Corner velocity matches MotionDynamicsProfileEngine output
Block starvation warnings generated for very short segments

units.title: Stage 3.3-3.4 — Look-ahead simulation + Multi-axis kinematics
steps: Wire MotionDynamicsProfileEngine.lookAhead(): simulate controller look-ahead buffer
N-block look-ahead: controller sees N blocks ahead and plans velocity profile accordingly
Adjust feed commands to match what the controller will actually achieve (reduce over-commanding)
Wire MultiAxisKinematicEngine for 5-axis programs
Singularity detection: flag blocks near gimbal lock (B≈0° for head-head, A≈90° for table-tilt)
Rotary axis velocity check: if rotary axis speed exceeds machine limit, reduce feed
RTCP pivot point compensation: adjust feed for tool center point control
Inverse time feed (G93) calculation for 5-axis blocks where linear feed is ambiguous
exit_conditions: Look-ahead simulation produces realistic feed profiles
5-axis singularity zones identified and feed reduced
Rotary axis speed limits enforced
G93 inverse time feed calculated correctly for 5-axis moves

units.title: Stage 3.5 — Controller feature injection (AICC, nano-smooth, look-ahead depth, Cycle32)
steps: Build controller feature injection logic — insert controller-specific optimization codes
Fanuc: G05.1 Q1 (AI Contour Control on), G05 P10000 (high-speed cycle), G08 P1 (smooth mode)
Siemens: CYCLE832(tolerance, mode) for HSC, COMPCAD for surface quality, COMPCURV for curvature comp
Heidenhain: FUNCTION TCPM (tool center point management), CYCLE 32 (tolerance definition), M128 (5-axis)
Haas: G187 P1/P2/P3 (smoothing modes — P1=rough fast, P2=medium, P3=finish smooth)
Mazak: G05.1 (MAZATROL Smooth), G61.1 (path blend)
Okuma: Super-NURBS activation, Machining Navi settings
Select features based on operation type: roughing→speed priority, finishing→surface priority
Insert feature codes at program start or per-operation as appropriate
Only inject features supported by the specific controller version (not all Fanucs have AICC)
exit_conditions: Fanuc 31i program gets G05.1 Q1 for finishing operations
Siemens 840D program gets CYCLE832 with appropriate tolerance
Haas program gets G187 P1 for roughing, P3 for finishing
Feature injection respects controller version capabilities
Features are NOT injected when controller doesn't support them

units.title: ControllerDialectEngine — Deep G-code dialect rules for 15+ controller families
steps: Create ControllerDialectEngine.ts (~2000 lines) with dialect rule system

Define ControllerDialect interface: { id, family, version, canned_cycles, work_offsets, sub_programs, tool_change, arc_format, comment_syntax, decimal_format, line_numbers, safe_start, program_end, rotary_axis_map, special_codes }
Implement dialect rules for 15 controller families:
Fanuc 0i-TF, Fanuc 30i-B, Fanuc 31i-B5 (differences in AICC, macro support)
Siemens 840D sl, Siemens ONE (ShopMill vs programGUIDE)
Heidenhain TNC 640, TNC 7 (plain text vs Klartext)
Haas NGC (Classic vs Next Gen differences)
Mazak SmoothAi, SmoothG, Matrix (conversational vs EIA/ISO)
Okuma OSP-P300, OSP-P500
Brother Speedio CNC-C00
Doosan Fanuc-variant
Hurco WinMax (conversational + NC)
Mitsubishi M80/M800
Fagor 8065
Canned cycle translation table: G81→CYCLE81(Siemens)→BORE1(Mazak)→MCALL/CYCLE(Heidenhain)
Work offset syntax: G54→$P_UIFR[1](Siemens)→DATUM(Heidenhain)→G15 H1(Mazak)
Sub-program conventions: M98 P/M99(Fanuc)→CALL/RET(Heidenhain)→EXTERN/L-call(Siemens)
Tool change sequences per machine type (vertical, horizontal, ATC magazine, turret)
Arc format rules: IJK incremental(Fanuc) vs absolute(some Siemens) vs R-word preference
Comment syntax: (parentheses)(Fanuc/Haas) vs ;semicolon(Siemens) vs ;comment(Heidenhain)
Decimal/format: leading zeros, trailing zeros, mandatory decimal point, block max length
Safe start blocks per controller (G90 G17 G21 G40 G80 order varies)
Program end: M30 vs M2 vs M30 with rewind vs END PGM (Heidenhain)
exit_conditions: 15 controller dialects defined with complete rule sets
Same toolpath produces syntactically correct G-code for Fanuc, Siemens, and Heidenhain
Canned cycle translation works for drilling, tapping, boring, reaming
Safe start blocks are controller-specific
40+ tests covering dialect differences

units.title: Stage 3.6 — Machine geometric error compensation
steps: Wire MachineGeometricAccuracyEngine: 21-error model per axis (positioning, straightness, angular)
Abbe principle: angular errors amplified by distance from measurement point
Volumetric error: HTM (Homogeneous Transformation Matrix) for total position error at any point
Thermal growth: δ = α·ΔT·L — compensate for temperature-induced positioning errors
If machine has ball-bar data in catalog, use actual measured errors
If no error data, use class-based estimates (ISO 230-2 accuracy classes)
For tolerance-critical operations: add error budget to tolerance check (predicted Cpk adjusts)
exit_conditions: Volumetric error calculated at work volume corners
Thermal compensation adjusts for shop temperature vs 20°C reference
Error budget feeds into Cpk prediction for realistic capability forecast
Graceful fallback for machines without measured error data
15+ tests
